texts: mixed: the date terms, 'in the morning', the wraith as the thing that faded and the cove's water as where it went all land cleanly, but the directional 'back' has no slot in the instruction set — it is neither a manner adverb nor a repetition marker — so the fact that the wraith was returning to where it came from is dropped. Put the return in a verb of its own: 'On day 131 of Year 1, in the morning, the wraith returned to the water of the Sunken Cove and faded into it.' Separately, 'day 131 of Year 1' goes into the translator's day-of-month slot, so day indices within one year cannot be ordered against each other; no rewording avoids that.

mixed: Hesper, the six-lantern group with its count, the 'drained' property distributed to each lantern, and the mire-essence are all recorded correctly, but 'during the following week' becomes an exact one-week gap from the wraith's fading — there is no forward-window form available, so the parse claims the refill happened precisely a week later rather than sometime inside that week. If an exact gap is acceptable, write 'A week later, Hesper refilled the mire-essence of the six drained lanterns.'; if you need the window, write 'After the wraith faded, Hesper refilled the mire-essence of the six drained lanterns.' and accept that the one-week bound goes unrecorded.

bad: 'returned to normal mist-light' forces the change-of-state shape, which asserts that each lantern IS mist-light — i.e. is itself a kind of light, which is false — while the group-level return event records nothing at all about what the lanterns returned to; the 'during the following week' window is stored as an exact one-week gap here too. Name the emitting verb, so the light is what the lanterns give off rather than what they are: 'A week later, the six lanterns again gave off normal mist-light.'
